evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A01251 entry: graphic history and variant analysis
evidence.text: The entry cites two oracle-bone forms (乙．八．七．二．二 and 庫．一．五．０．六) and several bronze forms, including examples from 豦簋, 牧師父簋, and 臣諫簋. It reports that the seal form resembles the Shuowen ancient graph. Separately, it judges 𢦢, a form with 戈, to be a later shape-confusion error based on resemblance to bronze 弟 and subsequent graph regularization. This is the dictionary editor’s analysis; it does not establish an unbroken development sequence from oracle bone to modern form.
evidence.title: 弟 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Kotobank, 日本国語大辞典 / 字通 entry
evidence.field: 字形; 訓義; 声系
evidence.text: The 字通 account interprets the graph as leather cord binding an object, associates it with successive/orderly binding, and says it was later used for sibling meaning. It lists sequence/order, younger person, humble self-reference, and other dictionary senses separately. It also lists 弟 among graphs in a sound series. This is a lexicographic interpretation, not independent proof of what the oldest form depicts or when each sense arose.
evidence.title: 弟(テイ)とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang character evolution database
evidence.field: database scope and 弟 query page
evidence.text: The database describes its holdings as including oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal, and regular-script forms. The queried 弟 page opened, but its rendered text exposed no individual form records or image URLs through this interface, so it did not yield a citable specific glyph image in this inspection.

evidence.text: The notice states that character images and character-attribute information obtained through the site’s query interface are made available under CC0 1.0. It does not grant rights to mirror the database, linked dictionary text, or other Academia Sinica sites.

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons file record, via Libre Wiki mirror search result
evidence.text: The accessible mirror describes 弟-bronze.svg as a bronze-script-style vector redraw and reports a public-domain dedication for the creator’s graphic. It identifies the image as a modern vector illustration, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact. The Commons file page itself could not be opened by the web tool, so this candidate is not included as a selected image.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the Xiaoxuetang character query and rights notice. Query page did not expose individual glyph/image entries in rendered text. Commons direct file access failed; a mirror search result described the public-domain modern redraw but was not sufficient for selecting it.

search_audit.query: 弟 character oracle-bone bronze etymology and early brother sense
search_audit.outcome: Opened the specialist database page and Kotobank entry. Kotobank supplies a graphic interpretation and separate glosses; no new independently dated early lexical witness was established in this invocation.

gaps: This invocation did not identify and inspect an individual Xiaoxuetang glyph image record, so no Xiaoxuetang image is proposed despite verifying its CC0 query-interface rights notice.

The Commons 弟-bronze.svg file page was inaccessible in the web tool. Its mirror description indicates a reusable modern vector redraw, but direct provenance and rights were not verified on the primary file page; no image is selected.

The inspected sources report early oracle-bone and bronze forms but do not establish a visually verified continuous graphic sequence or settle whether the early depicted element is a weapon shaft, peg, or binding arrangement.

No independent evidence in this invocation establishes the spoken name or ancient pronunciation of any proposed depicted implement. Reconstructions for 弟 cannot by themselves demonstrate a whole-graph sound loan.

No new dated contextual token for the sequence or sibling sense was established here. Repository dossier evidence reports a Western Zhou inscriptional 兄弟 example, while exact dating and the earliest order-sense attestation remain open.

limitations.text: No image is proposed because no candidate’s primary source page and image provenance were both successfully inspected to the requested standard in this invocation. Xiaoxuetang’s rights were confirmed, but its 弟 query returned no individual image details in rendered page text; Commons access to the specific 弟 file failed. The described Commons candidate is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.
